fulfillment.sourceText: Students completing the Stony Brook Curriculum (SBC) must complete a course that satisfies the "Write Effectively within One's Discipline" (WRTD) learning objective to graduate. The Upper Division Writing Requirement is consistent in most cases with the SBC learning outcomes for WRTD.

notes.text: Students seeking admission must write a Curricular Plan stating the two or three areas of concentration that satisfy the Course Distribution requirement and explaining how the selection serves their intellectual, professional, or personal goals. Courses not bearing the designator of the corresponding department or program must be justified in the Curricular Plan. Upon acceptance of the Plan by an MTD advisor, the student is admitted to the major. Changes in areas of concentration or additional courses require a revised Curricular Plan approved by a program advisor.
Students must see one of the MTD advisors to plan their individual program. Program Advisor: Catherine Marrone, Sociology. Program Coordinator: Diane West. Email: mtdmajor@stonybrook.edu.
The Multidisciplinary Studies major offers no courses of its own. An academic minor may also fulfill one of the student's areas.

Multidisciplinary Studies Honors Program (optional): open to majors with a cumulative GPA of 3.00 and a GPA of 3.50 in MTD areas of concentration. Requires a faculty mentor from one of the areas, an honors thesis, a proposal submitted by the start of the semester before graduation that includes two research courses or seminars, and an examining committee. An acceptable thesis satisfies the upper-division writing requirement. Honors are conferred if the thesis has sufficient merit and the other elements of the plan and GPA levels are met.
